Chapter 2: Building a Culture of Appreciation and Positive Regard
So, once you’ve laid the groundwork of friendship, what comes next? Well, it’s all about shaping the atmosphere between you and your partner—making it one where appreciation and respect really take center stage.
Let’s be honest: every relationship has its share of irritation, disappointment, or frustration. But here’s what sets thriving marriages apart—it's not that they never feel negative emotions, but that they have a strong, positive outlook that helps them bounce back.
Imagine this positive perspective as a special lens. Through it, you see your partner’s actions and intentions in a warmer, more generous light. When you regularly express admiration and gratitude, it actually becomes easier to give each other the benefit of the doubt.
Say your partner forgets to do a household chore. If your relationship is already full of kind words and appreciation, you’re way more likely to see that slip as just an oversight—not a deliberate slight.
So, how do you actually build this climate of appreciation? It’s simpler than you might think. Start by making it a habit to notice and acknowledge the good stuff. Maybe it’s a quick “thank you” for taking out the trash, or sharing a memory that always makes you smile together. These gestures aren’t just polite—they send a powerful message that says, “You matter to me.”
Here are a few practical ways you can strengthen appreciation in your relationship:
First, try setting aside some time to reflect on what you truly admire about your partner—and then tell them. Don’t keep those thoughts to yourself! Next, make it a point to express gratitude for both the little and big things. And when negative thoughts start to creep in, try to shift your focus back to your partner’s positive qualities or a kind moment you’ve shared.
There’s a concept that really drives this home—it’s called the “magic ratio.” Research suggests that happy, stable couples tend to have at least five positive interactions for every negative one.
Now, this isn’t about sweeping problems under the rug or pretending everything’s perfect. Instead, it’s about making sure the overall emotional climate is warm and supportive, even when challenges pop up.
Think about a couple who, even after a disagreement, make an effort to reconnect—maybe they share a laugh, show affection, or do something fun together. These moments are like emotional deposits, building up a reserve of goodwill for the tough times.
And here’s something that might surprise you—admiration and appreciation aren’t just personality traits. They’re skills you can actually practice. Even if you and your partner have grown a bit distant, you can reignite positive feelings by intentionally looking for and acknowledging each other’s strengths. Sure, it might feel a little awkward at first, especially if you’ve gotten used to focusing on the negatives. But stick with it, and you’ll start to see the emotional landscape of your relationship shift for the better.
Remember, building a culture of appreciation isn’t about ignoring problems or pretending they don’t exist. It’s about creating a space where both of you feel genuinely valued and respected. And when appreciation becomes a regular part of your daily life, it acts like a shield—helping your relationship handle the ups and downs that come your way.
